title: a Result PARAMETER whose only consumption is an unwrap inside a callback body is consumed, exactly as a local binding is
notes: specification/failures.mdx:190: 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' `entry` is unwrapped with postfix `!`, which is one of the five named acts, and the sentence conditions none of them on the function body the act is written in. 07-must-consume/result-parameter-must-be-consumed pins the refusal direction — a Result parameter nothing consumes is SMITHERS1302 — and this is its acceptance direction for a consumption that happens one function deeper. The printed line comes from `main` rather than from `forward`: the promise this case pins is that the program COMPILES, and `forward` cannot be called from authored `.sm` at all, because handing a Result to a user function is not consumption and the argument would be charged at its producer (07-must-consume/handing-a-result-collection-to-a-user-function-is-not-consumption). DELIBERATELY PAIRED with a-result-consumed-only-inside-a-callback-is-consumed, which is the identical consumption site reached from a local binding and which BOTH backends accept.

xfail.reason: the fork reports SMITHERS1302@14:25 — 'Result parameter must be consumed' — on a parameter that is consumed by `entry!` one line later, refusing the program. FOUND BY THIS LANE, not inherited: it surfaced as a second diagnostic on a callback-contract case and was then isolated with four probes that vary one thing at a time. The result of that isolation is what makes the verdict decisive rather than arguable: the fork ACCEPTS the byte-equivalent program in which `entry` is a LOCAL BINDING instead of a parameter (a-result-consumed-only-inside-a-callback-is-consumed, pass on both backends), so the fork's ownership walk does reach a consumption inside a nested function body — it simply does not reach it from the parameter entry point. The fork is therefore inconsistent with itself about the same consumption site, which is why the reference is right here rather than merely different. The contract of the callback is irrelevant to the trigger: it fires with a spelled `Result<string, Missing>` contract on the arrow, as here. Retire this marker when the fork's parameter-ownership walk descends into nested function bodies the way its binding walk already does.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx:190 — the five consumption forms are acts performed on the value ('returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it'), and no sentence on that page conditions any of them on the function body in which the act is written.
